records.source: וּשְׁלֹמֹ֗ה הָיָ֤ה מוֹשֵׁל֙ בְּכָל־הַמַּמְלָכ֔וֹת מִן־הַנָּהָר֙ אֶ֣רֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וְעַ֖ד גְּב֣וּל מִצְרָ֑יִם מַגִּשִׁ֥ים מִנְחָ֛ה וְעֹבְדִ֥ים אֶת־שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה כָּל־יְמֵ֥י חַיָּֽיו׃פ
records.gloss: And Solomon was ruling over all the kingdoms from the River [to the] land of [the] Philistines and to [the] border of Egypt; [they were] bringing tribute and serving Solomon all [the] days of his life.
pieces: Solomon ruled over all the kingdoms from the Euphrates River to the land of the Philistines and as far as the border of Egypt. They brought tribute and served Solomon throughout his life.

L.1: And Solomon was ruling over all the kingdoms from the River [to] the land of the Philistines and as far as the border of Egypt. They were bringing tribute and serving Solomon all the days of his life.

R.1: Solomon ruled over all the kingdoms from the Euphrates River to the land of the Philistines and all the way to the border of Egypt. These kingdoms paid him tribute and were under his rule as long as he lived.

decisions.choice: verse numbers: the Hebrew text begins chapter 5 here
decisions.reason: This translation numbers verses as the Hebrew text does. In the Hebrew text chapter 4 ends at verse 20, and the account of Solomon's rule, his court and his wisdom (5:1-14 here) is the start of chapter 5. Many Bibles number these verses 4:21-34, and so number the rest of this chapter (5:15-32 here) 5:1-18. The words are the same; only the numbers differ.

decisions.choice: the River: the Euphrates
decisions.reason: "The River" with the article names the great river of the north-east, the Euphrates, as in the promise of the land to Abraham and to Israel (Genesis 15:18; Deuteronomy 1:7; Joshua 1:4). Solomon's rule reached the borders that promise named.

decisions.choice: from the River to the land of the Philistines
decisions.reason: The Hebrew runs "from the River the land of the Philistines" with no word for "to". The sense is the span from the Euphrates to the Philistine coast; 2 Chronicles 9:26, which tells the same thing, has "to".

decisions.choice: bringing tribute and serving: subject kingdoms paying what they owed
decisions.reason: The word here translated "tribute" is the one used for a grain offering, but its first sense is a gift brought to a superior; between kingdoms it is the payment a subject king brings to his overlord (Judges 3:15; 2 Samuel 8:2, 6). "Serving" means being subject to him.

decisions.choice: the Euphrates River (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the river so that readers know which one "the River" means (m2).

decisions.choice: paid him tribute and were under his rule as long as he lived
decisions.reason: Readable says what "serving" meant for a kingdom (m4) and turns "all the days of his life" into everyday words.

records.heading: Solomon's rule and wisdom

records.source: וַיְהִ֥י לֶֽחֶם־שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה לְי֣וֹם אֶחָ֑ד שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים כֹּר֙ סֹ֔לֶת וְשִׁשִּׁ֥ים כֹּ֖ר קָֽמַח׃
records.gloss: And was [the] food of Solomon for one day thirty cors [of] fine flour and sixty cors [of] meal,
pieces: Solomon's provisions for a single day were {{units:about 180 bushels|thirty cors}} of fine flour and {{units:about 360 bushels|sixty cors}} of meal,

L.2: And Solomon's food for one day was thirty cors of fine flour and sixty cors of meal,

R.2: Every day Solomon's court used {{units:about 180 bushels|thirty cors}} of fine flour and {{units:about 360 bushels|sixty cors}} of ordinary flour.

decisions.choice: cor: the largest dry measure, about 6 bushels
decisions.reason: The cor held the same as a homer, ten ephahs (Ezekiel 45:14), about 6 bushels. Thirty cors is about 180 bushels and sixty about 360 bushels: food for a very large household every day.

decisions.choice: Solomon's food: the provisions for his whole court
decisions.reason: The word is "bread" in its wide sense of food. What follows feeds not Solomon alone but his household, his officials and everyone who ate at his table (verse 7).

decisions.choice: fine flour and meal: the best flour and ordinary flour
decisions.reason: The first word is the finely ground flour used for offerings and for the best bread (Leviticus 2:1); the second is plain ground meal (Judges 6:19; 1 Samuel 1:24).

decisions.choice: Solomon's court used (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable names the court, not Solomon alone, as the ones fed (m2).

records.source: עֲשָׂרָ֨ה בָקָ֜ר בְּרִאִ֗ים וְעֶשְׂרִ֥ים בָּקָ֛ר רְעִ֖י וּמֵ֣אָה צֹ֑אן לְ֠בַד מֵֽאַיָּ֤ל וּצְבִי֙ וְיַחְמ֔וּר וּבַרְבֻּרִ֖ים אֲבוּסִֽים׃
records.gloss: ten cattle fat and twenty cattle [of] pasture and a hundred sheep, apart from deer and gazelle and roebuck and fowl fattened.
pieces: ten fattened cattle, twenty cattle from the pasture and a hundred sheep and goats, besides deer, gazelles, roebucks and fattened birds.

L.3: ten fat oxen and twenty pasture oxen and a hundred sheep, apart from deer and gazelles and roebucks and fattened fowl.

R.3: They also needed ten stall-fed cattle, twenty cattle from the pastures, and a hundred sheep and goats. Besides these there were deer, gazelles, roe deer and fattened birds.

decisions.choice: fat cattle and pasture cattle: animals fattened in stalls and animals brought from grazing
decisions.reason: The first ten were fattened for the table; the next twenty came straight from the pastures. The contrast shows the two kinds of beef served at court.

decisions.choice: sheep: the flock, sheep and goats together
decisions.reason: The word names a flock of small livestock and covers both sheep and goats (Leviticus 1:10).

decisions.choice: fattened fowl: a kind of bird kept and fattened for eating
decisions.reason: The word for the birds is found only here, so the exact kind is not known. It may name geese, hens or some other fowl; the point is that they were fattened for the king's table.

decisions.choice: deer, gazelle and roebuck: wild game that Israel could eat
decisions.reason: These three wild animals are named among the clean animals in Deuteronomy 14:5. The third word probably names a roe deer or fallow deer.

decisions.choice: sheep (Literal); sheep and goats (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the single word; Balanced and Readable say that goats were included (m2).

records.source: כִּי־ה֞וּא רֹדֶ֣ה׀בְּכָל־עֵ֣בֶר הַנָּהָ֗ר מִתִּפְסַח֙ וְעַד־עַזָּ֔ה בְּכָל־מַלְכֵ֖י עֵ֣בֶר הַנָּהָ֑ר וְשָׁל֗וֹם הָ֥יָה ל֛וֹ מִכָּל־עֲבָרָ֖יו מִסָּבִֽיב׃
records.gloss: For he [was] ruling over all [the region] beyond the River, from Tiphsah and to Gaza, over all [the] kings beyond the River; and peace was to him from all his sides round about.
pieces: For he had dominion over the whole region west of the Euphrates, from Tiphsah to Gaza, over all the kings west of the Euphrates, and he had peace on every side all around him.

L.4: For he was ruling over all [the region] beyond the River, from Tiphsah as far as Gaza, over all the kings beyond the River; and he had peace on all his sides around [him].

R.4: This was because he ruled over all the land west of the Euphrates River, from the town of Tiphsah all the way to Gaza. All the kings of that region were under him, and he was at peace with all the nations around him.

decisions.choice: beyond the River: the lands west of the Euphrates
decisions.reason: The phrase looks at the land from the far side of the Euphrates, as the great empires to the east did; later it became the name of the province west of the river (Ezra 4:10-11). Here it means all the land from the Euphrates to the Mediterranean.

decisions.choice: Tiphsah and Gaza: the far north-east and the far south-west
decisions.reason: Tiphsah was a crossing place on the Euphrates; Gaza was the southernmost of the Philistine cities on the coast. Between them lies the whole region verse 1 describes.

decisions.choice: for: the reason for the great supplies
decisions.reason: The verse explains verses 2-3: such a court could be fed because so many lands were under Solomon's rule.

decisions.choice: peace on every side: the rest Yahweh had promised
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 12:10 promised rest from enemies all around, and 2 Samuel 7:1, 11 speaks of it under David. Solomon will point to this peace as the sign that the time has come to build the house (5:18).

decisions.choice: beyond the River (Literal); west of the Euphrates (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say which side of the river is meant, from the reader's point of view (m1).

decisions.choice: the town of Tiphsah (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says that Tiphsah is a town, since few readers will know the name.

records.source: וַיֵּשֶׁב֩ יְהוּדָ֨ה וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל לָבֶ֗טַח אִ֣ישׁ תַּ֤חַת גַּפְנוֹ֙ וְתַ֣חַת תְּאֵֽנָת֔וֹ מִדָּ֖ן וְעַד־בְּאֵ֣ר שָׁ֑בַע כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י שְׁלֹמֹֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And dwelt Judah and Israel in security, each under his vine and under his fig tree, from Dan and to Beersheba, all [the] days of Solomon.
pieces: Judah and Israel lived in safety, {{gender:everyone|every man}} under {{gender:their|his}} own vine and under {{gender:their|his}} own fig tree, from Dan to Beersheba, all through Solomon's lifetime.

L.5: And Judah and Israel dwelt in security, each under his vine and under his fig tree, from Dan as far as Beersheba, all the days of Solomon.

R.5: As long as Solomon lived, the people of Judah and Israel were safe, from Dan in the far north to Beersheba in the far south. Every family could sit in peace under its own grapevine and its own fig tree.

decisions.choice: each under his vine and under his fig tree: living in peace and plenty on one's own land
decisions.reason: To sit under one's own vine and fig tree is a picture of a settled life without fear, eating the fruit of one's own land (Micah 4:4; Zechariah 3:10; 2 Kings 18:31).

decisions.choice: from Dan to Beersheba: the whole land, north to south
decisions.reason: Dan was the northernmost town of Israel and Beersheba the southernmost; the pair stands for the whole country (Judges 20:1; 1 Samuel 3:20).

decisions.choice: each: every household, men and women alike
decisions.reason: The word means "each man", but it is used for every person in the land; the whole people lived in safety, not the men only.

decisions.choice: everyone ... their own (Balanced)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the gender setting, since the whole people is meant (m3); Literal keeps the single Hebrew word as "each".

decisions.choice: every family could sit in peace; in the far north ... in the far south (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable explains both pictures (m1, m2): who lived under the vines, and where Dan and Beersheba lay.

records.source: וַיְהִ֣י לִשְׁלֹמֹ֗ה אַרְבָּעִ֥ים אֶ֛לֶף אֻרְוֺ֥ת סוּסִ֖ים לְמֶרְכָּב֑וֹ וּשְׁנֵים־עָשָׂ֥ר אֶ֖לֶף פָּרָשִֽׁים׃
records.gloss: And were to Solomon forty thousand stalls [of] horses for his chariots and twelve thousand horsemen.
pieces: Solomon had 40,000 stalls of horses for his chariots, and 12,000 horsemen.

L.6: And Solomon had 40,000 stalls of horses for his chariots, and 12,000 horsemen.

R.6: Solomon had 40,000 stalls for the horses that pulled his chariots, and he had 12,000 horsemen.

decisions.choice: 40,000 stalls, as the Hebrew text reads
decisions.reason: 2 Chronicles 9:25, which tells the same thing, has 4,000 stalls, and 1 Kings 10:26 gives Solomon 1,400 chariots, which fits the smaller number better. A copyist may have changed one number; this translation keeps the number the Hebrew text of Kings has.

decisions.choice: horsemen: riders, or possibly chariot horses
decisions.reason: The word usually means horsemen, but it can also name the horses themselves; beside the stalls and chariots either sense is possible (10:26).

decisions.choice: many horses: what the law warned a king against
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 17:16 told Israel's king not to gather many horses for himself. The narrator lists Solomon's horses without comment here, but the reader is meant to remember that law (10:26-29; 11:1-4).

records.source: וְכִלְכְּלוּ֩ הַנִּצָּבִ֨ים הָאֵ֜לֶּה אֶת־הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה וְאֵ֧ת כָּל־הַקָּרֵ֛ב אֶל־שֻׁלְחַ֥ן הַמֶּֽלֶךְ־שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה אִ֣ישׁ חָדְשׁ֑וֹ לֹ֥א יְעַדְּר֖וּ דָּבָֽר׃
records.gloss: And supplied these officers King Solomon and all the [one] approaching to [the] table of King Solomon, each [in] his month; not they let lack a thing.
pieces: These officers provided for King Solomon and for everyone who came to King Solomon's table, each in his month. They saw to it that nothing was lacking.

L.7: And these officers supplied King Solomon and all who came near to the table of King Solomon, each [in] his month; they let nothing be lacking.

R.7: Solomon's twelve district officers each took a month to provide food for King Solomon and for everyone who ate at the king's table. They made sure there was always enough.

decisions.choice: these officers: the twelve district officers of 4:7-19
decisions.reason: Solomon had divided the land into twelve districts, each under an officer who supplied the king's household for one month of the year (4:7). The account of Solomon's rule in verses 1-6 interrupts the list, and this verse returns to it.

decisions.choice: all who came near to the king's table: everyone fed at court
decisions.reason: To come to the king's table means to eat at the king's expense: his family, officials, guests and those he honored (2:7; 2 Samuel 9:7, 13).

decisions.choice: twelve district officers each took a month (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says who "these officers" are and how the months were shared out (m1).

records.source: וְהַשְּׂעֹרִ֣ים וְהַתֶּ֔בֶן לַסּוּסִ֖ים וְלָרָ֑כֶשׁ יָבִ֗אוּ אֶל־הַמָּקוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִֽהְיֶה־שָּׁ֔ם אִ֖ישׁ כְּמִשְׁפָּטֽוֹ׃ס
records.gloss: And the barley and the straw for the horses and for the steeds they brought to the place where it was there, each according to his assignment.
pieces: They also brought barley and straw for the horses and the swift horses to the place where it was needed, each according to his assignment.

L.8: And the barley and the straw for the horses and for the swift steeds they would bring to the place where it should be, each according to his assignment.

R.8: They also brought barley and straw for the horses, including the fast chariot horses. Each officer took his share to the place where it was needed.

decisions.choice: steeds: swift horses
decisions.reason: This word names fast horses used for chariots and for royal messengers (Esther 8:10, 14; Micah 1:13).

decisions.choice: the place where it should be: wherever the supplies were needed
alternatives: the place where the king was
the place where the horses were stationed
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "the place where it would be there" and does not say what "it" is. It may mean wherever the king was, or wherever the horses were kept (9:19; 10:26), or simply the place set for each delivery. The sense is that each officer brought his share to where it was required.

decisions.choice: according to his assignment: the share laid on each officer
decisions.reason: The word often means "judgment" or "custom"; here it is the rule or quota set for each officer.

decisions.choice: fast chariot horses; each officer (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable explains the kind of horse (m1) and says that "each" means each officer.

records.source: וַיִּתֵּן֩ אֱלֹהִ֨ים חָכְמָ֧ה לִשְׁלֹמֹ֛ה וּתְבוּנָ֖ה הַרְבֵּ֣ה מְאֹ֑ד וְרֹ֣חַב לֵ֔ב כַּח֕וֹל אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־שְׂפַ֥ת הַיָּֽם׃
records.gloss: And gave God wisdom to Solomon and understanding very much, and breadth of heart like the sand which [is] on [the] shore of the sea.
pieces: God gave Solomon wisdom and very great understanding, and a breadth of mind as vast as the sand on the seashore.

L.9: And God gave Solomon wisdom and understanding very great, and breadth of heart like the sand that [is] on the shore of the sea.

R.9: God made Solomon very wise and gave him great understanding. There was no end to what his mind could take in. It was like the sand on the seashore.

decisions.choice: breadth of heart: a mind of wide range
decisions.reason: The heart is the seat of thought and understanding. A broad heart takes in a great many things; the same picture of breadth stands behind verses 12-13.

decisions.choice: like the sand on the seashore: past counting
decisions.reason: The sand of the sea is a picture of what cannot be measured (Genesis 22:17); 4:20 used it for the people of Judah and Israel. Here it is used for Solomon's understanding.

decisions.choice: God gave wisdom: the answer to Solomon's prayer
decisions.reason: This fulfills what God promised at Gibeon: "a wise and discerning heart" (3:9, 12).

decisions.choice: heart (Literal); mind (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "mind", since the heart here is the place of understanding (m1).

records.source: וַתֵּ֨רֶב֙ חָכְמַ֣ת שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה מֵֽחָכְמַ֖ת כָּל־בְּנֵי־קֶ֑דֶם וּמִכֹּ֖ל חָכְמַ֥ת מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And was great [the] wisdom of Solomon more than [the] wisdom of all [the] sons of [the] east and more than all [the] wisdom of Egypt.
pieces: Solomon's wisdom was greater than the wisdom of all the peoples of the east and greater than all the wisdom of Egypt.

L.10: And the wisdom of Solomon was greater than the wisdom of all the {{gender:people|sons}} of the east and than all the wisdom of Egypt.

R.10: Solomon was wiser than all the people of the east and wiser than all the people of Egypt, though they were famous for their wisdom.

decisions.choice: the people of the east and Egypt: nations famous for wisdom
decisions.reason: The desert peoples to the east (Job 1:3) and Egypt (Genesis 41:8; Isaiah 19:11-12) were known for their wise men and their collections of sayings. Solomon's wisdom outshone the best that was known.

decisions.choice: though they were famous for their wisdom (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable adds why these nations are named (m1).

records.source: וַיֶּחְכַּם֮ מִכָּל־הָֽאָדָם֒ מֵאֵיתָ֣ן הָאֶזְרָחִ֗י וְהֵימָ֧ן וְכַלְכֹּ֛ל וְדַרְדַּ֖ע בְּנֵ֣י מָח֑וֹל וַיְהִֽי־שְׁמ֥וֹ בְכָֽל־הַגּוֹיִ֖ם סָבִֽיב׃
records.gloss: And he was wise more than all the human, more than Ethan the Ezrahite and Heman and Calcol and Darda, sons of Mahol; and was his name in all the nations round about.
pieces: He was wiser than anyone else, wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, Calcol and Darda, the sons of Mahol. His fame spread to all the surrounding nations.

L.11: And he was wiser than all humankind, than Ethan the Ezrahite and Heman and Calcol and Darda, the sons of Mahol; and his name was in all the nations around.

R.11: He was wiser than anyone, even wiser than the famous wise men Ethan the Ezrahite, Heman, Calcol and Darda, the sons of Mahol. People in all the nations around Israel heard about him.

decisions.choice: Ethan, Heman, Calcol and Darda: wise men well known in their day
decisions.reason: Ethan the Ezrahite and Heman are named in the titles of Psalms 89 and 88. 1 Chronicles 2:6 lists Ethan, Heman, Calcol and Dara as sons of Zerah of Judah. Their fame is the measure Solomon's wisdom is set against.

decisions.choice: sons of Mahol: their father's name, or a description
decisions.reason: Mahol may be the name of their father. The word also means "dance", so "sons of Mahol" may describe them as belonging to a guild of musicians or singers, which would fit the psalm titles that name Ethan and Heman.

decisions.choice: his name: his fame
decisions.reason: A person's name stands for his reputation (1 Samuel 18:30).

decisions.choice: the famous wise men (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says why these four are named (m1).

records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֕ר שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֖ים מָשָׁ֑ל וַיְהִ֥י שִׁיר֖וֹ חֲמִשָּׁ֥ה וָאָֽלֶף׃
records.gloss: And he spoke three thousand proverbs, and were his songs five and a thousand.
pieces: He spoke 3,000 proverbs, and his songs numbered 1,005.

L.12: And he spoke 3,000 proverbs, and his songs were 1,005.

R.12: He spoke 3,000 wise sayings, and he made up 1,005 songs.

decisions.choice: proverbs: short sayings of wisdom, often comparisons
decisions.reason: The word names a saying that sets one thing beside another to teach a lesson, as in the book of Proverbs (Proverbs 1:1; 10:1; 25:1).

decisions.choice: 1,005 songs, as the Hebrew text reads
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation gives 5,000 songs. The Hebrew number is kept here.

decisions.choice: his songs: the songs linked with Solomon
decisions.reason: The Song of Songs (1:1) and Psalms 72 and 127 carry Solomon's name in their titles.

decisions.choice: wise sayings; made up (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable explains "proverbs" (m1) and says that the songs were his own.

records.source: וַיְדַבֵּר֮ עַל־הָֽעֵצִים֒ מִן־הָאֶ֨רֶז֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּלְּבָנ֔וֹן וְעַד֙ הָאֵז֔וֹב אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֹצֵ֖א בַּקִּ֑יר וַיְדַבֵּר֙ עַל־הַבְּהֵמָ֣ה וְעַל־הָע֔וֹף וְעַל־הָרֶ֖מֶשׂ וְעַל־הַדָּגִֽים׃
records.gloss: And he spoke about the trees, from the cedar which [is] in Lebanon and to the hyssop which comes out in the wall; and he spoke about the animals and about the birds and about the creeping things and about the fish.
pieces: He spoke about trees, from the cedar in Lebanon to the hyssop growing out of the wall, and he spoke about animals, birds, creeping things and fish.

L.13: And he spoke about the trees, from the cedar that [is] in Lebanon as far as the hyssop that comes out in the wall; and he spoke about the beasts and about the birds and about the creeping things and about the fish.

R.13: He spoke about trees and plants, from the great cedars of Lebanon to the little hyssop plant that grows out of cracks in a wall. He also spoke about animals, birds, creatures that crawl on the ground, and fish.

decisions.choice: spoke about: spoke of, in his sayings and teaching
decisions.reason: The words may mean that he described plants and animals, or that he drew his proverbs from them, as Proverbs 6:6 and 30:24-31 do. Either way his wisdom took in the whole living world.

decisions.choice: from the cedar to the hyssop: from the greatest plant to the least
decisions.reason: The cedar of Lebanon was the tallest and noblest tree people knew; hyssop was a small bushy plant that could grow in cracks of a wall (Exodus 12:22). The pair includes everything between.

decisions.choice: beasts, birds, creeping things and fish: the creatures of Genesis 1
decisions.reason: The four groups are the living creatures over which humankind was given rule (Genesis 1:26; 9:2).

decisions.choice: trees and plants; little hyssop plant; creatures that crawl on the ground (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable shows that hyssop is a small plant (m2) and explains "creeping things".

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ מִכָּל־הָ֣עַמִּ֔ים לִשְׁמֹ֕עַ אֵ֖ת חָכְמַ֣ת שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה מֵאֵת֙ כָּל־מַלְכֵ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁמְע֖וּ אֶת־חָכְמָתֽוֹ׃ס
records.gloss: And they came from all the peoples to hear [the] wisdom of Solomon, from all [the] kings of the earth who had heard his wisdom.
pieces: People came from all the nations to hear Solomon's wisdom; they came on behalf of all the kings of the earth, who had heard how wise he was.

L.14: And they came from all the peoples to hear the wisdom of Solomon, from all the kings of the earth who had heard of his wisdom.

R.14: People came from every nation to listen to Solomon's wisdom. Kings all over the world had heard how wise he was, and they sent people to hear him.

decisions.choice: from all the kings of the earth: sent by kings
decisions.reason: "From the kings" most likely means that people came on behalf of kings, as their envoys. Some kings came themselves, as the queen of Sheba did (10:1-13).

decisions.choice: the world comes to hear Solomon's wisdom
decisions.reason: This is told at length in 10:1-13 and again in 10:23-24.

decisions.choice: they sent people to hear him (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says how people came "from" the kings (m1).

records.source: וַ֠יִּשְׁלַח חִירָ֨ם מֶֽלֶךְ־צ֤וֹר אֶת־עֲבָדָיו֙ אֶל־שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה כִּ֣י שָׁמַ֔ע כִּ֥י אֹת֛וֹ מָשְׁח֥וּ לְמֶ֖לֶךְ תַּ֣חַת אָבִ֑יהוּ כִּ֣י אֹהֵ֗ב הָיָ֥ה חִירָ֛ם לְדָוִ֖ד כָּל־הַיָּמִֽים׃ס
records.gloss: And sent Hiram king of Tyre his servants to Solomon, for he had heard that him they had anointed [as] king in place of his father; for a friend had been Hiram to David all the days.
pieces: Hiram king of Tyre sent his officials to Solomon when he heard that Solomon had been anointed king in his father's place, for Hiram had always been a friend of David.

L.15: And Hiram king of Tyre sent his servants to Solomon, for he had heard that they had anointed him king in place of his father; for Hiram had been a friend to David all the days.

R.15: Hiram, the king of Tyre, had always been a friend of David. So when he heard that Solomon had been anointed king to take his father's place, he sent his officials to Solomon.

decisions.choice: verse numbers: this verse is 5:1 in many Bibles
decisions.reason: This translation numbers verses as the Hebrew text does. Hebrew 5:1-14 is numbered 4:21-34 in many Bibles, so the account of Hiram and the building materials (5:15-32 here) is numbered 5:1-18 there. The words are the same; only the numbers differ.

decisions.choice: Hiram king of Tyre: ruler of the great Phoenician port
decisions.reason: Tyre was a trading city on the coast north of Israel, built partly on an island. Hiram had sent cedar and craftsmen to build David's house (2 Samuel 5:11).

decisions.choice: a friend: an ally bound by a treaty
decisions.reason: The word means "one who loves". Between kings it is the language of alliance: a king who "loves" another is his faithful treaty partner. Hiram's friendship with David now passes to David's son.

decisions.choice: they had anointed him: he had been anointed
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "they anointed" without naming who; the sense is that Solomon had been made king (1:39).

decisions.choice: servants (Literal); officials (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: These are a king's envoys, so Balanced and Readable call them officials, as these books do for a king's servants.

records.heading: Hiram supplies wood for the temple

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה אֶל־חִירָ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And sent Solomon to Hiram, saying,
pieces: Solomon sent word to Hiram:

L.16: And Solomon sent to Hiram, saying,

R.16: Solomon sent this message to Hiram:

decisions.choice: Solomon's message: told more fully in Chronicles
decisions.reason: 2 Chronicles 2:2-15 gives a longer form of this exchange of letters between Solomon and Hiram.

decisions.choice: sent word (Balanced); sent this message (Readable)
decisions.reason: Hebrew says only "sent ... saying"; Balanced and Readable supply what was sent.

records.source: אַתָּ֨ה יָדַ֜עְתָּ אֶת־דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֗י כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יָכֹל֙ לִבְנ֣וֹת בַּ֗יִת לְשֵׁם֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֔יו מִפְּנֵ֥י הַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר סְבָבֻ֑הוּ עַ֤ד תֵּת־יְהוָה֙ אֹתָ֔ם תַּ֖חַת כַּפּ֥וֹת רַגְלָֽי׃
records.gloss: You know David my father, that not he was able to build a house for [the] name of Yahweh his God because of the war which surrounded him, until gave Yahweh them under [the] soles of his feet.
pieces: "You know that my father David could not build a house for the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God because of the wars waged against him on every side, until {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} put his enemies under the soles of his feet.

L.17: "You know David my father, that he was not able to build a house for the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God because of the warfare that surrounded him, until {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} put them under the soles of his feet.

R.17: "You know that my father David could not build a temple where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God would be worshiped. Enemies were fighting against him on every side, until {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} let him defeat them all.

decisions.choice: his feet
decisions.reason: The Hebrew tradition records two forms of this word. The letters as written read "my feet"; the vowels and the reading handed down with them give "his feet". The word data used here analyzes the written letters. "His feet" fits the sentence, which speaks of David's wars, and is followed here.

decisions.choice: put them under the soles of his feet: gave him full victory over them
decisions.reason: To put enemies under someone's feet is to make them wholly defeated, as a conqueror set his foot on a beaten king (Joshua 10:24; Psalm 8:7; 110:1).

decisions.choice: a house for the name of Yahweh: the place where his name would dwell
decisions.reason: As in 3:2, the house is for Yahweh's name, the place Deuteronomy said he would choose for his name to live (Deuteronomy 12:5, 11).

decisions.choice: David could not build because of war
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 7 tells how David wished to build a house for Yahweh and was told that his son would build it. 1 Chronicles 22:8 gives another side of the reason: David had shed much blood in war.

decisions.choice: his enemies (Balanced); enemies (Readable)
decisions.reason: Hebrew says "them", meaning the enemies at war with David; Balanced and Readable name them.

decisions.choice: a temple where the LORD his God would be worshiped; let him defeat them all (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says "temple" for the house, explains "for the name of the LORD" (m3) and puts the picture of m2 in plain words.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֕ה הֵנִ֨יחַ יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהַ֛י לִ֖י מִסָּבִ֑יב אֵ֣ין שָׂטָ֔ן וְאֵ֖ין פֶּ֥גַע רָֽע׃
records.gloss: And now has given rest Yahweh my God to me from round about; there is no adversary and there is no occurrence evil.
pieces: But now {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God has given me rest all around. I have no adversary and face no misfortune.

L.18: And now {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God has given me rest all around; there is no adversary and no evil occurrence.

R.18: But now {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God has given me peace on every side. No enemy is attacking me, and no disaster threatens us.

decisions.choice: adversary: an opponent, not a proper name
decisions.reason: The word means an enemy or opponent. Later Yahweh raises up such adversaries against Solomon (11:14, 23, 25), the same word.

decisions.choice: rest on every side: the time to build the house
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 12:10-11 links rest from enemies with the place Yahweh would choose. With that rest given (5:4), Solomon sees the time for the house has come.

decisions.choice: evil occurrence: misfortune, a disaster
decisions.reason: The phrase names any harmful event that might strike, such as war, plague or famine.

decisions.choice: peace; no enemy is attacking me; no disaster threatens us (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable puts "rest" and the two nouns into plain words.

records.source: וְהִנְנִ֣י אֹמֵ֔ר לִבְנ֣וֹת בַּ֔יִת לְשֵׁ֖ם יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֑י כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר׀דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אֶל־דָּוִ֤ד אָבִי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר בִּנְךָ֗ אֲשֶׁ֨ר אֶתֵּ֤ן תַּחְתֶּ֨יךָ֙ עַל־כִּסְאֶ֔ךָ הֽוּא־יִבְנֶ֥ה הַבַּ֖יִת לִשְׁמִֽי׃
records.gloss: And here I [am] saying to build a house for [the] name of Yahweh my God, just as spoke Yahweh to David my father, saying, Your son whom I will set in your place on your throne, he will build the house for my name.
pieces: So I intend to build a house for the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} told my father David: 'Your son, whom I will put on your throne in your place, will build the house for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name.'

L.19: And so I am intending to build a house for the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to David my father, saying, 'Your son, whom I will set on your throne in your place, he will build the house for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name.'

R.19: So I plan to build a temple where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God will be worshiped. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} promised my father David, 'Your son, whom I will make king after you, will build the temple to honor {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name.'

decisions.choice: I am saying to build: I intend to build
decisions.reason: "To say" can mean to say to oneself, to plan or decide (Exodus 2:14; 2 Samuel 21:16).

decisions.choice: your son will build the house: Yahweh's promise to David
decisions.reason: Solomon quotes the promise of 2 Samuel 7:12-13, in which Yahweh told David that his son would build a house for his name.

decisions.choice: he will build: he and no other
decisions.reason: The pronoun "he" is written out, which gives weight to it: it is David's son, not David, who will build.

decisions.choice: so (Literal, Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word often rendered "behold" here draws a conclusion from verse 18; "so" says that in modern English.

decisions.choice: temple; make king after you; to honor my name (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says "temple" for the house, explains setting a son on the throne, and puts "for my name" in plain words.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֡ה צַוֵּה֩ וְיִכְרְתוּ־לִ֨י אֲרָזִ֜ים מִן־הַלְּבָנ֗וֹן וַֽעֲבָדַי֙ יִהְי֣וּ עִם־עֲבָדֶ֔יךָ וּשְׂכַ֤ר עֲבָדֶ֨יךָ֙ אֶתֵּ֣ן לְךָ֔ כְּכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר תֹּאמֵ֑ר כִּ֣י׀אַתָּ֣ה יָדַ֗עְתָּ כִּ֣י אֵ֥ין בָּ֛נוּ אִ֛ישׁ יֹדֵ֥עַ לִכְרָת־עֵצִ֖ים כַּצִּדֹנִֽים׃
records.gloss: And now command, and let them cut for me cedars from the Lebanon, and my servants will be with your servants, and [the] wage of your servants I will give to you according to all that you say; for you know that there is not among us a man knowing to cut wood like the Sidonians.
pieces: So now give orders for cedars from Lebanon to be cut for me. My servants will work with your servants, and I will pay you whatever wages you set for your servants. You know that none of us knows how to cut timber as well as the Sidonians do."

L.20: And now command that they cut cedars for me from Lebanon, and my servants will be with your servants; and I will give you wages for your servants according to all that you say. For you know that there is no one among us who knows how to cut timber like the Sidonians."

R.20: So now order your men to cut down cedar trees in Lebanon for me. My workers will work beside yours, and I will pay your workers whatever you ask. As you know, none of my people can cut timber as skillfully as the Sidonians can."

decisions.choice: the Sidonians: the people of Phoenicia
decisions.reason: Sidon was the older of the two great Phoenician cities, and "Sidonians" was a name for the Phoenicians as a whole, Tyre included (16:31; Deuteronomy 3:9). They were famous for working wood and for seafaring.

decisions.choice: cedars from Lebanon: the finest building timber
decisions.reason: The cedars of the Lebanon mountains were tall, straight and lasting, and kings of many lands sought them for palaces and temples. "The Lebanon" has the article in Hebrew because it names the mountain range.

decisions.choice: servants: the men who work for each king
decisions.reason: Here the word means the king's men set to work on the timber, Solomon's and Hiram's alike, not court officials.

decisions.choice: servants (Literal, Balanced); workers, men (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable names these servants by the work they do (m3).

records.source: וַיְהִ֞י כִּשְׁמֹ֧עַ חִירָ֛ם אֶת־דִּבְרֵ֥י שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה וַיִּשְׂמַ֣ח מְאֹ֑ד וַיֹּ֗אמֶר בָּר֤וּךְ יְהוָה֙ הַיּ֔וֹם אֲשֶׁ֨ר נָתַ֤ן לְדָוִד֙ בֵּ֣ן חָכָ֔ם עַל־הָעָ֥ם הָרָ֖ב הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And it was, when heard Hiram [the] words of Solomon, and he rejoiced greatly and said, Blessed [be] Yahweh today, who has given to David a son wise over the people the great the this.
pieces: When Hiram heard Solomon's words, he was delighted and said, "Blessed be {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} today, who has given David a wise son to rule over this great people!"

L.21: And it happened, when Hiram heard the words of Solomon, that he rejoiced greatly and said, "Blessed [be] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} today, who has given to David a wise son over this great people."

R.21: Hiram was very glad when he heard Solomon's message. He said, "Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} today! He has given David a wise son to rule over this great nation."

decisions.choice: a foreign king blesses Yahweh
decisions.reason: Hiram praises Israel's God by name, as the queen of Sheba later does (10:9). Kings honored one another's gods in the courtesy of alliances; the words show respect for Yahweh, but do not say that Hiram left his own gods.

decisions.choice: today: the day of the blessing
decisions.reason: "Today" goes with Hiram's blessing: on hearing the news, he blesses Yahweh now. It could also be read with what follows, "who has today given David a wise son"; the sense is much the same.

decisions.choice: to rule over (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Hebrew says "a wise son over this people"; Balanced and Readable add "to rule", which the word "over" implies.

decisions.choice: Praise the LORD (Readable)
decisions.reason: To "bless" Yahweh means to praise and thank him; Readable says "praise".

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח חִירָם֙ אֶל־שְׁלֹמֹ֣ה לֵאמֹ֔ר שָׁמַ֕עְתִּי אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־שָׁלַ֖חְתָּ אֵלָ֑י אֲנִ֤י אֶֽעֱשֶׂה֙ אֶת־כָּל־חֶפְצְךָ֔ בַּעֲצֵ֥י אֲרָזִ֖ים וּבַעֲצֵ֥י בְרוֹשִֽׁים׃
records.gloss: And sent Hiram to Solomon, saying, I have heard what you sent to me; I will do all your desire concerning timber of cedars and concerning timber of cypresses.
pieces: Then Hiram sent word to Solomon: "I have received the message you sent me. I will do all you wish in the matter of cedar timber and cypress timber.

L.22: And Hiram sent to Solomon, saying, "I have heard what you sent to me. I will do all your desire concerning cedar timber and concerning cypress timber.

R.22: Then Hiram sent this message to Solomon: "I have received your message. I will give you all the cedar and cypress logs you want.

decisions.choice: cypress: a tall evergreen tree, perhaps juniper or fir
decisions.reason: The tree cannot be named with certainty. It was a strong evergreen of Lebanon, used with cedar for floors, doors and ships (6:15, 34; Ezekiel 27:5), probably a cypress or a juniper.

decisions.choice: all your desire: everything you wish
decisions.reason: The word means what someone wants or delights in. Hiram agrees to all that Solomon asked; verse 23 adds what Hiram wants in return.

decisions.choice: sent word (Balanced); sent this message (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 16.

records.source: עֲ֠בָדַי יֹרִ֨דוּ מִן־הַלְּבָנ֜וֹן יָ֗מָּה וַ֠אֲנִי אֲשִׂימֵ֨ם דֹּבְר֤וֹת בַּיָּם֙ עַֽד־הַמָּק֞וֹם אֲשֶׁר־תִּשְׁלַ֥ח אֵלַ֛י וְנִפַּצְתִּ֥ים שָׁ֖ם וְאַתָּ֣ה תִשָּׂ֑א וְאַתָּה֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה אֶת־חֶפְצִ֔י לָתֵ֖ת לֶ֥חֶם בֵּיתִֽי׃
records.gloss: My servants will bring down from the Lebanon to [the] sea, and I will make them rafts in the sea to the place which you send to me, and I will break them up there, and you will carry [them] away; and you will do my desire by giving [the] food of my household.
pieces: My servants will bring the logs down from Lebanon to the sea, and I will have them tied into rafts and sent by sea to the place you name. There I will have them taken apart, and you can carry them away. And you will meet my wishes by providing food for my household."

L.23: My servants will bring [them] down from Lebanon to the sea, and I will make them into rafts on the sea [to go] to the place that you send [word of] to me, and I will break them up there, and you will carry [them] away. And you will do my desire by giving food for my household."

R.23: My workers will bring the logs down from the mountains of Lebanon to the sea. I will tie them together into rafts and float them along the coast to whatever place you choose. There I will have the rafts taken apart, and your men can take the logs away. In return, I want you to supply food for my royal household."

decisions.choice: rafts by sea: floating the logs down the coast
decisions.reason: The logs were tied together and floated or towed along the coast to a port near Israel; 2 Chronicles 2:15 names Joppa. From there they were carried overland to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: you will carry them away; you will do my desire: each king's part in the bargain
decisions.reason: The repeated "you" sets out what Solomon must do: take charge of the timber at the port, and give Hiram what he wants in return. Hiram uses the same word "desire" for his own wish that Solomon used for Solomon's (verse 22).

decisions.choice: food for my household: grain for Tyre's royal court
decisions.reason: Tyre had little farmland of its own and depended on grain from Israel and Judah (Ezekiel 27:17; Acts 12:20). Hiram asks for food for his court in exchange for the timber.

decisions.choice: servants (Literal, Balanced); workers (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 20.

decisions.choice: tie them together; float them along the coast; your men; in return (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable spells out how rafts were made and moved (m1), who would carry the logs, and that the food was payment for the timber (m2).

records.source: וַיְהִ֨י חִיר֜וֹם נֹתֵ֣ן לִשְׁלֹמֹ֗ה עֲצֵ֧י אֲרָזִ֛ים וַעֲצֵ֥י בְרוֹשִׁ֖ים כָּל־חֶפְצֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And was Hiram giving to Solomon timber of cedars and timber of cypresses, all his desire.
pieces: So Hiram supplied Solomon with all the cedar timber and cypress timber he wished for.

L.24: And Hiram was giving Solomon cedar timber and cypress timber, all his desire.

R.24: So Hiram gave Solomon all the cedar and cypress logs he wanted.

decisions.choice: was giving: a supply that went on over time
decisions.reason: The verb form describes continuing action: Hiram kept sending timber while the work went on.

decisions.choice: all his desire: all that Solomon wanted
decisions.reason: "His" is Solomon: Hiram kept the promise of verse 22.

records.source: וּשְׁלֹמֹה֩ נָתַ֨ן לְחִירָ֜ם עֶשְׂרִים֩ אֶ֨לֶף כֹּ֤ר חִטִּים֙ מַכֹּ֣לֶת לְבֵית֔וֹ וְעֶשְׂרִ֥ים כֹּ֖ר שֶׁ֣מֶן כָּתִ֑ית כֹּֽה־יִתֵּ֧ן שְׁלֹמֹ֛ה לְחִירָ֖ם שָׁנָ֥ה בְשָׁנָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And Solomon gave to Hiram twenty thousand cors [of] wheat [as] food for his household, and twenty cors [of] oil beaten; thus gave Solomon to Hiram year by year.
pieces: Solomon gave Hiram {{units:about 120,000 bushels|20,000 cors}} of wheat as food for his household, and {{units:about 1,200 gallons|twenty cors}} of pressed olive oil. Solomon gave this to Hiram year after year.

L.25: And Solomon gave Hiram 20,000 cors of wheat [as] food for his household, and twenty cors of beaten oil. Thus Solomon would give to Hiram year by year.

R.25: Each year Solomon gave Hiram {{units:about 120,000 bushels|20,000 cors}} of wheat to feed his household and {{units:about 1,200 gallons|twenty cors}} of the finest olive oil.

decisions.choice: twenty cors of oil, as the Hebrew text reads
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation reads "twenty thousand baths of oil", and 2 Chronicles 2:9, which describes the agreement differently and adds barley and wine for the woodcutters, also has 20,000 baths. A bath is a tenth of a cor, so the Greek reading is a hundred times larger. The Hebrew text of Kings is followed here.

decisions.choice: beaten oil: the finest olive oil
decisions.reason: Oil made by pounding olives gently, rather than pressing them in a mill, ran clear and pure. It was the oil for the lamp of the tabernacle (Exodus 27:20).

decisions.choice: cor as a measure of grain and of oil
decisions.reason: For wheat the cor is about 6 bushels (verse 2), so 20,000 cors is about 120,000 bushels. For oil it is ten baths (Ezekiel 45:14); a bath is about 6 gallons, so twenty cors is about 1,200 gallons.

decisions.choice: beaten oil (Literal); pressed olive oil (Balanced); the finest olive oil (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the olive and say what kind of oil this was (m2).

records.source: וַיהוָ֗ה נָתַ֤ן חָכְמָה֙ לִשְׁלֹמֹ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּר־ל֑וֹ וַיְהִ֣י שָׁלֹ֗ם בֵּ֤ין חִירָם֙ וּבֵ֣ין שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה וַיִּכְרְת֥וּ בְרִ֖ית שְׁנֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And Yahweh gave wisdom to Solomon, just as he had spoken to him; and there was peace between Hiram and between Solomon, and they made a covenant, the two of them.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave wisdom to Solomon, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had promised him. Hiram and Solomon were at peace, and the two of them made a treaty with each other.

L.26: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave wisdom to Solomon, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had spoken to him; and there was peace between Hiram and Solomon, and the two of them made a covenant.

R.26: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave Solomon wisdom, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had promised. Hiram and Solomon lived at peace, and the two kings made a treaty.

decisions.choice: as he had spoken to him: the promise at Gibeon
decisions.reason: Yahweh promised Solomon wisdom in the dream at Gibeon (3:12). The narrator sets the treaty with Hiram beside that promise: the wise handling of the alliance is part of the wisdom Yahweh gave.

decisions.choice: peace and a covenant: a formal alliance between two kings
decisions.reason: Between nations, "peace" means friendly relations, and a "covenant" is a sworn treaty with duties on both sides.

decisions.choice: covenant (Literal); treaty (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Between two kings the covenant is a treaty, and Balanced and Readable say so (m2).

records.source: וַיַּ֨עַל הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֛ה מַ֖ס מִכָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיְהִ֣י הַמַּ֔ס שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף אִֽישׁ׃
records.gloss: And raised King Solomon forced labor from all Israel, and was the forced labor thirty thousand men.
pieces: King Solomon drafted forced labor from all Israel, and the labor force numbered 30,000 men.

L.27: And King Solomon raised forced labor from all Israel, and the forced labor was 30,000 men.

R.27: King Solomon forced 30,000 men from all over Israel to work for him.

decisions.choice: forced labor: work that people were made to do for the king
decisions.reason: The word names a body of workers made to labor without choice, and the system of labor itself (Joshua 16:10; Judges 1:28). Adoniram was over it (4:6; 5:28).

decisions.choice: from all Israel: a burden on Solomon's own people
decisions.reason: 9:22 says that Solomon made no Israelite a slave; that seems to mean they were not made permanent slaves, as the Canaanites were (9:20-21), while these men served in turns (5:28). The burden still weighed on the people, and it was the complaint that split the kingdom after Solomon's death (12:4, 18).

decisions.choice: raised (Literal); drafted (Balanced); forced ... to work (Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb "made go up" means calling men up for service; Balanced says "drafted" and Readable says plainly what was done.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלָחֵ֣ם לְבָנ֗וֹנָה עֲשֶׂ֨רֶת אֲלָפִ֤ים בַּחֹ֨דֶשׁ֙ חֲלִיפ֔וֹת חֹ֚דֶשׁ יִהְי֣וּ בַלְּבָנ֔וֹן שְׁנַ֥יִם חֳדָשִׁ֖ים בְּבֵית֑וֹ וַאֲדֹנִירָ֖ם עַל־הַמַּֽס׃ס
records.gloss: And he sent them to Lebanon, ten thousand in a month, shifts; a month they were in Lebanon, two months in his house; and Adoniram [was] over the forced labor.
pieces: He sent them to Lebanon in shifts of 10,000 a month. They spent a month in Lebanon and two months at home. Adoniram was in charge of the forced labor.

L.28: And he sent them to Lebanon, 10,000 a month in shifts; a month they were in Lebanon, two months at his home. And Adoniram [was] over the forced labor.

R.28: He sent them to Lebanon in groups of 10,000 men. Each group worked in Lebanon for one month and then went home for two months. Adoniram was in charge of these workers.

decisions.choice: shifts: each man served one month in three
decisions.reason: The 30,000 men were split into three groups of 10,000. Each group worked a month in Lebanon and then went home for two, so every man served four months of the year.

decisions.choice: Adoniram: the officer over the forced labor
decisions.reason: He is named among Solomon's officials (4:6). The Adoram of 2 Samuel 20:24 and 1 Kings 12:18, who was stoned when he went to the northern tribes, is very likely the same man.

decisions.choice: at his home: each man at his own home
decisions.reason: "His" refers to each worker.

decisions.choice: groups; each group ... went home; these workers (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable explains how the shifts worked (m1).

records.source: וַיְהִ֧י לִשְׁלֹמֹ֛ה שִׁבְעִ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף נֹשֵׂ֣א סַבָּ֑ל וּשְׁמֹנִ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף חֹצֵ֥ב בָּהָֽר׃
records.gloss: And were to Solomon seventy thousand carrying burden and eighty thousand cutting in the mountain,
pieces: Solomon also had 70,000 men who carried loads and 80,000 who cut stone in the hill country,

L.29: And Solomon had 70,000 bearers of burdens and 80,000 stonecutters in the hills,

R.29: Solomon also had 70,000 men to carry loads and 80,000 men to cut stone in the hills.

decisions.choice: cutting in the mountain: quarrying stone in the hills
decisions.reason: The word means one who hews, here stone (verse 31). "The mountain" means the hill country, where the stone was quarried.

decisions.choice: the carriers and stonecutters: who these workers were
decisions.reason: 2 Chronicles 2:16-17 says these 150,000 were foreigners living in Israel, which agrees with 9:20-22. Kings itself does not say who they were here.

decisions.choice: men who ... (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Hebrew uses the participles alone, "carrying" and "cutting"; Balanced and Readable add "men".

records.heading: Solomon's workers

records.source: לְ֠בַד מִשָּׂרֵ֨י הַנִּצָּבִ֤ים לִשְׁלֹמֹה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־הַמְּלָאכָ֔ה שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֖ים וּשְׁלֹ֣שׁ מֵא֑וֹת הָרֹדִ֣ים בָּעָ֔ם הָעֹשִׂ֖ים בַּמְּלָאכָֽה׃
records.gloss: apart from [the] chiefs of the officers of Solomon who [were] over the work, three thousand and three hundred, the [ones] ruling over the people doing the work.
pieces: besides Solomon's 3,300 chief officers who were over the work and directed the people who did it.

L.30: apart from the chiefs of Solomon's officers who [were] over the work, 3,300, who ruled over the people doing the work.

R.30: There were also 3,300 foremen who were in charge of the work and gave orders to the workers.

decisions.choice: 3,300, as the Hebrew text reads
decisions.reason: 2 Chronicles 2:1, 17 gives 3,600 overseers, and 1 Kings 9:23 names 550 more chief officers. The numbers may count different ranks, or a figure may have changed in copying. The Hebrew of this verse is followed.

decisions.choice: chiefs of the officers: foremen over the work gangs
decisions.reason: These "officers" are not the twelve district officers of verse 7 but the men set over the building work, who drove the laborers.

decisions.choice: chiefs (Literal); chief officers (Balanced); foremen (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word often rendered "princes" or "officials" here names work supervisors, so these books' usual wording for it would mislead (m2).

records.source: וַיְצַ֣ו הַמֶּ֡לֶךְ וַיַּסִּעוּ֩ אֲבָנִ֨ים גְּדֹל֜וֹת אֲבָנִ֧ים יְקָר֛וֹת לְיַסֵּ֥ד הַבָּ֖יִת אַבְנֵ֥י גָזִֽית׃
records.gloss: And commanded the king, and they quarried stones great, stones costly, to lay the foundation [of] the house, stones of hewn [stone].
pieces: At the king's command they quarried great, costly stones, so that the foundation of the house could be laid with dressed stone.

L.31: And the king commanded, and they quarried great stones, costly stones, to lay the foundation of the house, stones of dressed [stone].

R.31: The king gave orders, and the workers cut large, valuable blocks of stone from the quarries. They shaped the blocks to lay the foundation of the temple.

decisions.choice: quarried: pulled stone out of the rock
decisions.reason: The verb means to pull up or break out; with stones it means quarrying them (Ecclesiastes 10:9).

decisions.choice: costly stones: stones of fine quality
decisions.reason: The word means precious or valuable. Here it describes large, high-grade building stone, as again in 7:9-11.

decisions.choice: dressed stone: stone cut and squared
decisions.reason: The word names stone cut to shape with tools. The stones were dressed at the quarry, so that no iron tool was heard at the building site (6:7).

decisions.choice: the workers; from the quarries; shaped the blocks; temple (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says who quarried the stone and what dressed stone is (m3), and says "temple" for the house.

records.source: וַֽיִּפְסְל֞וּ בֹּנֵ֧י שְׁלֹמֹ֛ה וּבֹנֵ֥י חִיר֖וֹם וְהַגִּבְלִ֑ים וַיָּכִ֛ינוּ הָעֵצִ֥ים וְהָאֲבָנִ֖ים לִבְנ֥וֹת הַבָּֽיִת׃פ
records.gloss: And cut Solomon's builders and Hiram's builders and the Gebalites, and they prepared the timber and the stones to build the house.
pieces: Solomon's builders and Hiram's builders and the men of Gebal shaped the stones, and they prepared the timber and the stone for building the house.

L.32: And Solomon's builders and Hiram's builders and the Gebalites cut [them], and they prepared the timber and the stones to build the house.

R.32: Solomon's builders and Hiram's builders worked with men from the city of Gebal. They cut and shaped the stones and got the logs and the stones ready for building the temple.

decisions.choice: the Gebalites: men of the Phoenician city of Gebal
decisions.reason: Gebal, later called Byblos, was a port north of Sidon; its craftsmen were known for skilled work (Ezekiel 27:9; Joshua 13:5).

decisions.choice: cut: shaped stone by cutting
decisions.reason: The verb is used for cutting stone to shape, as for the tablets of the law (Exodus 34:1). Its object is not stated; the stones of verse 31 are meant.

decisions.choice: the stones (Balanced, Readable); the men of Gebal; the city of Gebal
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name what was cut (m2) and say that the Gebalites came from a city.
